Best Time to Visit Madagascar

Travel Guide The Madagascar Collection 9 min read

Madagascar is unlike anywhere else on Earth. Home to incredible wildlife, pristine beaches, towering baobab trees and landscapes found nowhere else, this island nation offers unforgettable experiences throughout the year. Choosing the best time to visit, however, can make a significant difference to your trip — this guide will help you decide when to go based on what you most want to experience.

When Is the Best Time to Visit Madagascar?

The best time to visit Madagascar is generally during the dry season, from April to November. During these months temperatures are pleasant, roads are more accessible and wildlife viewing opportunities are excellent. That said, the ideal time for your own trip depends entirely on what you want to see and do.

SeasonMonthsBest For
Dry SeasonApril – NovemberWildlife, hiking, sightseeing, beach holidays
Whale SeasonJuly – SeptemberHumpback whale watching
BirdwatchingSeptember – DecemberMigratory and endemic birds
Green SeasonDecember – MarchLush landscapes, photography, fewer tourists
Lemur ViewingYear-roundDifferent species active throughout the year

Madagascar Weather by Season

April to June · One of the Best Times to Visit

As the rainy season comes to an end, Madagascar transforms into a lush green paradise. Rivers are flowing, landscapes are vibrant and temperatures are comfortable across much of the island. This period offers excellent wildlife viewing, beautiful scenery after the rains, comfortable temperatures, fewer visitors than peak season and wonderful photography. National parks are particularly stunning during these months, making it a favourite time for nature enthusiasts and photographers.

July to September · Peak Travel Season

For many travellers, July to September is the absolute best time to visit Madagascar. The weather is dry and sunny across most regions, making it ideal for exploring the island's diverse landscapes. Highlights include whale watching, exceptional hiking conditions, comfortable daytime temperatures, excellent road conditions and prime wildlife viewing. This is also the busiest travel season, so booking accommodation and tours well in advance is recommended.

October to November · Wildlife Lovers' Paradise

October and November offer some of the best wildlife experiences in Madagascar. Many animals become more active as temperatures rise, and this is a fantastic time to spot baby lemurs, chameleons, reptiles, rare birds and endemic wildlife. The weather remains relatively dry while visitor numbers are often lower than during peak winter months. For photographers and wildlife enthusiasts, this period is often considered one of Madagascar's hidden gems.

December to March · The Green Season

Madagascar's summer months bring warmer temperatures and increased rainfall. While some travellers avoid this period, it has real advantages: fewer tourists, lower accommodation rates, spectacular green landscapes, dramatic photography and excellent birdwatching. Some remote roads may become difficult to access due to heavy rains and certain parks may have limited accessibility, but if you're planning a beach holiday or luxury island escape, many coastal areas still offer excellent experiences during this season.

Over 90% of Madagascar's wildlife is found nowhere else on Earth — including its famous lemurs.

Best Time for Wildlife

Madagascar is famous for its extraordinary biodiversity, with the overwhelming majority of its species endemic to the island.

Best Time to See Lemurs

Lemurs can be seen throughout the year, but many travellers find April to November offers the best overall viewing conditions. During spring and early summer (October–November) many species become especially active, and visitors may even spot young lemurs.

Best Time to See Whales

July to September is whale-watching season in Madagascar. Humpback whales migrate through Madagascar's waters, creating one of the most spectacular marine wildlife experiences in the Indian Ocean.

From July to September, migrating humpback whales pass through Madagascar's warm coastal waters.

Best Time for Birdwatching

Birdwatchers should consider September to December, when many endemic and migratory species are active. Madagascar is home to over 280 bird species, making it one of Africa's premier birding destinations.

Best Time for the Beaches

If your dream holiday includes turquoise waters and white-sand beaches, consider visiting between May and November. Popular beach destinations enjoy sunny weather, lower humidity, calm seas and excellent diving and snorkelling conditions — perfect for combining wildlife adventures with a relaxing beach escape.

Between May and November, Madagascar's coastline offers calm seas and superb snorkelling.

Best Time for the National Parks

Most travellers come to Madagascar for its incredible national parks, and the best months for park visits are generally April to November. The reasons: dry hiking trails, easier wildlife spotting, better road access and comfortable temperatures. Whether you're exploring rainforests, canyons, limestone formations or baobab forests, the dry season offers the most reliable conditions.

The dry season is the most reliable window for exploring Madagascar's lush forests and reserves.

Month-by-Month Summary

  • January — Warm and rainy. Best for lush scenery and birdwatching.
  • February — One of the wettest months. Travel to remote regions may be challenging.
  • March — Rainfall begins to decrease. Landscapes remain beautifully green.
  • April — Excellent weather returns. One of the best months for nature lovers.
  • May — Dry, sunny and comfortable. Ideal for touring.
  • June — Great wildlife viewing and pleasant temperatures.
  • July — Peak season begins. Excellent for whale watching.
  • August — One of the most popular months to visit.
  • September — Fantastic weather and outstanding wildlife opportunities.
  • October — Excellent for lemurs, reptiles and photography.
  • November — Warm temperatures and active wildlife.
  • December — Beginning of the rainy season, but still suitable for many coastal holidays.

So, What Is the Best Time to Visit?

If you're looking for the best overall combination of weather, wildlife viewing and accessibility, we recommend travelling between April and November. For whale watching, choose July to September. For wildlife photography, October and November are exceptional. For lush landscapes and fewer crowds, consider April, May or early June.

"Madagascar is a year-round destination — every season offers its own unique experiences."
